articleTitle: Face frontalization GAN with self-supervised learning for pose-invariant facial recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Despite impressive milestones achieved by generative models such as Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) in synthesizing faces, maintaining face identity remains a major challenge for most face recognition system. In this paper, we propose a Self-supervised Face Frontalization GAN (SF-GAN), which produces a frontal face image from a profile image. We designed a profile method to preserve identity information and fine details in high-resolution that focus on pose feature space, which helps SF-GAN reconstruct high-frequency face texture details. SF-GAN switches key facial regions between the input image and its reconstructed version to produce more realistic images. Furthermore, we introduce an orthogonal constraint to our generator that penalizes redundant latent representations, resulting in a more diverse pose appearance details. While the discriminator is designed with a mechanism of facial awareness for each facial region to improve overall model performance. FaceNet and MTCNN are then used to extract correlated face features in order to determine the accuracy of face recognition. Our evaluations are based on the Multi-PIE and CAS-PEAL datasets. Results showed that SF-GAN achieved a better face quality visualization and rank-1 face identification.

articleTitle: Adversarial and Self-Adaptive Domain Decomposition Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for High order Differential Equations with Discontinuities
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: The technique of solving differential equations using Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) has received extensive attention and application. However, employing neural networks with continuous activation functions throughout the domain makes it difficult to accurately approximate functions with discontinuities. The original domain decomposition PINNs rely on prior knowledge, as well as manual decomposition of the domain and manual handle of interface conditions between subnetworks. To address this issue, this paper proposes Adversarial and Self-Adaptive Domain Decomposition Physics-Informed Neural Networks (AS-PINNs), which employ adversarial methods to automatically adjust the boundary positions of subdomains and capture different discontinuities. The self-adaptive domain decomposition makes AS-PINNs to be tailored to high order problems by addressing issues arising from the singularity of differentiation at discontinuities.

articleTitle: A Social Value Orientation-Based Priority Swapping Algorithm for Efficient Autonomous Intersection Management
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Efficient coordination of autonomous vehicles at intersections is essential for minimizing delays and ensuring safety. Traditional approaches such as First-Come-First-Serve (FCFS) often overlook the potential benefits of vehicle cooperation. In this work, we propose a novel Social Value Orientation (SVO)based algorithm that enhances intersection management by allowing vehicles to cooperate based on their social preferences, ranging from egoistic to prosocial behavior. Our algorithm enables pairwise reservation swapping, improving system-wide performance without compromising individual utility. Simulation results demonstrate a significant reduction in vehicle wait times, especially in systems with a higher proportion of prosocial vehicles. This work presents a promising step toward socially-compliant, efficient coordination policies for future autonomous traffic systems.

articleTitle: Promoting culture in Peru through a graph-based recommender system
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Culture and its dissemination are an important aspect of the identity of a community or country and its population. Peru has a wide diversity of cultural manifestations, but its population tends to overlook them and governmental institutions do not provide efficient support for their promotion and development, limiting their scope and citizen participation. This paper proposes a solution model for a web application that uses recommendation systems to promote culture in Peru. There are many similar proposals that make use of this technology, the most outstanding of them being due to the efficency of the graph neural networks implemented in them. The solution consists of five components and requires web scraping tools and APis to keep the collected data updated. The model presented is a convolutional graph network (GCN) that, when trained with the Amazon Products Electronics dataset, achieves favorable results in terms of recommendation generation. The Machine Learning model designed achieves the mean absolute error less than 1.6 at the level of the experiments performed and it is integrated with three other components that make up our overall proposal at the design level. There are three items that can be developed in future work in order to complete its implementation and improve the efficiency of the components.

articleTitle: Improving Voice-Based Emotion Recognition Using Convolutional Neural Networks: Integrating RAVDESS and JL Corpus Datasets
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Voice-based emotion recognition has garnered significant attention in data science, with applications in fields such as psychology, gaming, healthcare, and customer service. This study explores emotion detection using voice recordings from the JL Corpus and RAVDESS datasets, employing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to classify emotions such as neutral, calm, happy, sad, angry, fearful, disgusted, and surprised. Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) are used for feature extraction. The CNN model achieved 73% accuracy on the RAVDESS dataset, though it underperformed compared to previous studies using multimodal data. However, combining the JL Corpus with RAVDESS improved accuracy to $85 \%$ and significantly enhanced precision and recall. Misclassifications between similar emotions highlight the limitations of amplitude-based features, suggesting the need for more advanced feature extraction techniques. This research contributes to the growing body of work in emotion recognition, emphasizing the potential for dataset integration and feature refinement to improve model performance.

articleTitle: Semantic Segmentation and Pathology Localization in Lung Ultrasound Images Using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Significant progress has been made to leverage machine learning towards decision support diagnosis from ultrasound in medical imaging. Due to the continuous challenges associated with evolving characteristics of COVID-19, the availability of fast, safe, and highly sensitive diagnostic tools is imperative. Where ultrasound imaging has been proven superior to X-rays and CT scans, the main limitation to its use is operator dependency and experience. In this study, we propose a novel transfer learning and semantic segmentation framework for automatic detection and localization of multiple lung pathologies in Lung Ultrasound images. The proposed framework allows better interpretation and explanation of the model decisions, with clear visualization and localization of the different pathologies. The experimental evaluation of the proposed framework was done on an open-source Lung ultrasound imaging dataset which is labeled and annotated by team of radiologists. The proposed approach was validated using other benchmarks models for comparison in terms of DICE coefficients at 0.98 and IOU Score at 0.97 which outperforms the other benchmark models quite significantly. This provides interpretation of the reasoning behind the decision made by the model leading to higher rates of acceptance with clinicians.

articleTitle: Leveraging Semantic Similarity for Non-Conformity management in industrial environments
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: In this work we explore the use of semantic similarity techniques to enhance the management of Non-Conformity in emerging industrial environments. Small and new companies lack historical data which makes unfeasible the application of Machine Learning-based solutions for data processing. Regarding this, we investigate the usage of training-independent semantic similarity techniques for Non-Conformity matching. Specifically, we compared two text vectorization methods, Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency and the Word2vec model combined with the cosine distance algorithm to reduce the amount of Non-Conformity to be processed by human specialists automatically finding the reports that point out the same quality issue.

articleTitle: EnviroBot: Towards a Transfer Learning and Computer Vision-based Herbicide Applicator Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: The proliferation of broadleaf weeds on lawns is a prevalent issue in Australia, impacting the aesthetic appeal of lawns and obstructing walking areas. Traditional manual herbicide spraying poses risks to human health, while indiscriminate herbicide application results in environmental pollution and wastage. To address this, we developed EnviroBot, a transfer learning and computer vision-based herbicide applicator prototype, to identify and locate Plantain weeds in lawns accurately. Our prototype utilised a web camera, illuminator, and shade cover to capture training images annotated and used for training with YOLOv8’s nano model. Transfer learning was employed to fine-tune the YOLOv8 model, resulting in an overall precision of $78 \%$ after 391 epochs of training. Live testing demonstrated the model’s effectiveness in identifying and localising Plantain weeds precisely and suitable for real-time usage. Future improvements could involve employing multispectral cameras and expanding the training dataset.

articleTitle: Context Aware Cyberbullying Classification Using Network Science
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: This research investigates the use of network science measures to enhance cyberbullying detection. Traditional detection algorithms rely on machine learning to classify content as ‘bullying’ based solely on textual analysis. However, these approaches often miss context, leading to incorrect classifications. Limited research has been done on incorporating network measures based on connections, to provide social context on platforms. This study integrates network features with textbased features, following a cyberbullying definition from the literature that includes aggression, repetition, harmful intent, power imbalance, and peer visibility. The results demonstrate that combining network context features and text features leads to higher accuracy in cyberbullying classification than methods relying only on text.

articleTitle: Development of Mobile Application for Skin Cancer Detection Using Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Skin cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, emphasizing the critical need for accurate and timely diagnosis. The current clinical treatments are time-consuming and susceptible to human error, which can delay treatment and affect patient outcomes. This research addresses these challenges by making two major contributions to the field. Firstly, four fine-tuned deep neural models; MobileNetV2, MobileNetV3, EfficientNetV2, and ResNet50; were evaluated across three distinct experimental settings to explore their potential in accurately classifying skin lesions. Among the models tested, MobileNetV3 outperformed the others, achieving the highest accuracy of 80.17% in categorizing four types of skin cancer in dermoscopic images and 79.17% in clinical images. Secondly, the study indicated that the development of an accessible mobile application capable of detecting skin cancer at its early stages is crucial. This app leverages the MobileNetV3 model to provide a quick and reliable tool for early diagnosis, thereby broadening access to life-saving interventions and reducing the burden of treatments on healthcare systems.

articleTitle: Face Expression Recognition on Ojek Online for Safety Improvement Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: During COVID-19, many workers were laid off because the company was struggling with financial challenges. Hence, laid-off workers have switched professions to become Ojek Online (Ojol) drivers because they have the flexibility to work with adequate income. In addition, the COVID-19 period has changed people’s behavior to choose Ojol because it is easy and practical. The growing number of demands has the risk of accidents due to fatigue and lack of adequate rest time. This study aims to implement deep learning methods such as Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Bidirectional Long-Short Term Memory (BiLSTM), and Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) to minimize the accident risk with face expression recognition. It will also compare the three methods to find the best method. About 350 primary data were collected from the participants’ questionnaires, grouped into seven facial expression classes: angry, sad, happy, sleepy, surprised, afraid, and neutral. Afterwards, the augmentation was implemented to solve the imbalance dataset problem. At the EDA stage, the positive correlation between object size, area, and resolution received a score of 1, while the negative correlation of the attribute’s light intensity and saturation was - 0.428. The result of performance evaluation on the three methods is that the BiGRU method achieved the best value with accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score values, respectively, 0.67, 0.69, 0.71, and 0.69. From this study, BiGRU is recommended as the best method. In addition, increasing the number of datasets and facial expression groups is necessary, as well as combining deep learning methods with evolutionary algorithms to find the best parameters to improve model performance automatically.

articleTitle: PM4Tree: A Scriptable Parametric Modeling Interface for Decorative Tree Design Using PM4VR
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: This paper introduces PM4Tree, a scriptable parametric modeling interface tailored for the procedural generation of decorative trees in Virtual Reality (VR). Built upon the PM4VR framework, PM4Tree combines parametric design principles with intuitive scripting capabilities to allow users to design a wide range of aesthetically pleasing and mathematically inspired tree structures. By extending PM4VR’s framework, PM4Tree enables seamless integration of parametric tree design interface into environments, making it suitable for applications in interior design, digital content generation, spatial computing, game development, and VR experiences. This interface empowers users to rapidly iterate on decorative tree designs, adjusting parameters such as branch patterns, leaf density, and tree shape, thus offering high levels of flexibility and creative control.

articleTitle: Vision Transformer-based Deep Learning Model for Leather Species Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Identifying the species of animal leather becomes a prominent factor in assessing the quality of the leather goods and also in defending the endangered species. Unlike convolutional neural network (CNN)-based deep learning (DL) architectures, the present work employs vision transformer (ViT)based modelling for leather species identification with a diverse set of images from different regions of the leather. It uses a self-attention mechanism to relate the whole image region enabling the model to analyse the complex pattern efficaciously. An input leather image is divided into disjoint patches and each patch is transformed into vectors. Positional encodings are added to patch embeddings to furnish the spatial hierarchies of each patch inside the image. The resulting vector series are passed through a transformer encoder which aids in capturing the global dependencies. Finally, the species prediction is done by passing the output of a transformer encoder to a multilayer perceptron head. The proposed model achieved a prediction accuracy of 96.3%. Moreover, the experimental analysis compares and proves the superiority of the ViT-based approach over the state-of-the-art CNNs.

articleTitle: Automatic generation of training data for semantic segmentation using game engine
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Semantic segmentation is a traditional task in computer vision that has been widely used in many fields. However, there are still many challenges in generating large and diverse pixel-level labeled datasets, such as difficulty in data collection, inaccurate manual annotation, and high cost. To address these issues, this paper proposes an innovative method based on a game engine for automatically generating semantic segmentation training data. By flexibly controlling the generation of scene objects and camera configurations, this method significantly simplifies the data collection and annotation process, effectively expands the scale of training data, and improves model performance. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the method in computer-generated images and real-world scene images, verifying its feasibility in improving the performance of semantic segmentation models. This paper provides a reliable alternative to the traditional semantic segmentation data generation process and lays the foundation for improving the generalization ability of models.

articleTitle: QLoRA-Based Fine-Tuning of LLMs on Multiple Medical Reasoning Tasks to Enhance their Comprehension of Clinical Notes
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Clinical notes pertinent to patient discharge summaries are crucial for support and decision-making during medical ministrations. LLMs (Large Language Models) have demonstrated exceptional capabilities in natural language processing. Therefore, exploiting their prowess in coherent knowledge retrieval is desired for clinical decision-making assistance. This study aims to enhance the performance of LLMs in comprehending the intricacies of clinical notes by fine-tuning them on the following medical reasoning tasks: 1) Summarization; 2) Relation Extraction; 3) Coreference Resolution; 4) Temporal Information Extraction; 5) Question-Answering; 6) Abbreviation Expansion; 7) Paraphrasing; 8) Named Entity Recognition. We have investigated the ability of 3 state-of-the-art LLMs to grasp medical reasoning efficiently when fine-tuned by computationally inexpensive QLoRA (Quantised Low-Rank Adaptation) technique. Among Mistral-2 (7B), Llama-3 (8B), and Llama-2 (13B), Llama-3(8B) proves to be adept for medical reasoning by outperforming the other LLMs on average over all the tasks when assessed with ROUGE (Recall Oriented Understudy for Gist Evaluation) and BLEU (Bilingual Evaluation Understudy) metric. Further, we also compare Llama-3’s efficacy post-fine-tuning and pre-fine-tuning on the ability to recall and be precise in generating relevant answers to questions concerning all tasks.

articleTitle: Foreign Exchange Rate Forecast by a Large Language Model Integrated with Trend Description
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a large language model to forecast the direction of change in a foreign exchange rate. The input of the proposed model is textual information as a prompt, whereas that of conventional forecast models is numerical information. A recent trend in the exchange rate is added to input textual information to enhance forecast accuracy. GPT-2 is adopted as our large language model and is fine-tuned using training data. The effectiveness of the proposed model is empirically examined using actual data.

articleTitle: Using Explainability Techniques to Assist Android Malware Detection Models in Resisting Adversarial Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: This study explores using Function Call Graphs (FCGs) to generate adversarial examples to improve the robustness of Android malware detection models. With Android holding a market share of up to 70% [1], its applications are frequent targets for attacks. To counter increasingly sophisticated threats, this research employs machine learning and deep learning, using FCGs to create adversarial samples that can evade detection with up to a 95% evasion rate. We focuses on simulated annealing, and explainable AI (XAI) techniques for generating these samples and uses adversarial training to balance accuracy and robustness in detection models. Adversarial training helps models identify such adversary samples, while XAI provides insights into the models’ decision-making processes, enhancing their ability to detect malicious apps. This approach achieves an F1-Score of 94% in standard training and 91% with adversarial training, outperforming simulated annealing (86%) in resisting unknown adversarial samples, with XAI showing an average detection rate of 92%.

articleTitle: Indian Sign Language Recognition System
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: This paper presents an Indian Sign Language (ISL) recognition system, leveraging advanced deep learning techniques to address the communication barriers faced by the hearing-impaired community. The system is designed to recognize and interpret ISL gestures into corresponding text or speech, facilitating effective interaction between hearing-impaired individuals and the broader population. Our approach involves a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture, specifically ResNet-50, trained on the ISL dataset. Key features include image preprocessing, data augmentation, and real-time gesture recognition. Experimental results demonstrate the system’s high accuracy and robustness, showcasing its potential for practical deployment in various real-world applications. This work contributes significantly to the field of assistive technology, aiming to enhance the inclusivity and accessibility of communication for the hearing-impaired community in India.

articleTitle: Ensemble Learning: An Indispensable Ingredient for Enhancing Regression Tree Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: It is a common knowledge that ensemble learning can be used to improve performance of predictive models, but it may not work well under certain situations, such as with stable learners. Thus, ensemble approach may come across to some practitioners as only an option when searching for an accurate model. In this paper, we highlight a situation where ensemble learning is not an option. Particularly with regression trees, we argue that ensemble learning is indispensable in enhancing the estimation performance. Regression trees, while popular, are known to produce rough regression surfaces, resulting in imprecise estimations when applied as a single individual tree model. This paper shows that ensemble learning addresses this issue by combining predictions from a diverse set of regression trees, effectively smoothing the regression surface. Experimental results across five real-world datasets show that ensemble learning consistently reduces predictive errors of regression trees, and the performance of single regression trees are consistently inferior. This underscores the efficacy of ensemble learning in smoothing prediction surfaces and reducing errors. For stable learners that do not suffer from the problem of rough prediction surfaces, such as Linear Regression and Support Vector Regression, ensemble learning offers limited to no improvements over single models. These findings emphasize the necessity of applying ensemble learning whenever regression trees are employed.

articleTitle: Towards a General Type 2 Fuzzy Reasoning Approach to Modeling Modifiable Dementia Risk Factors
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Dementia is the most critical neurodegenerative disease that gradually destroys memory and other cognitive functions. Hence early detection is utmost necessary and to build an effective detection model, it is required to understand its type, symptoms, stages and causes, as well as diagnosis methodologies. Many risk factors for dementia, identified from observational studies, are potentially modifiable; based on a large-scale review of observational studies, the Lancet Commission of Dementia Prevention, Intervention and Care estimated that approximately 40% of cases of clinically classified dementia could be attributed to twelve key modifiable dementia risk factors (MDRFs). Based on this evidence, the aim of this paper is to develop a fuzzy reasoning model that allows giving linguistic values to the data and information obtained from patients and giving an evaluation based on fuzzy rules; thus being able to interpret from these modifiable risk factors the percentage of risk that the patient has of increasing them according to their characteristics and lifestyle. The fuzzy reasoning is developed using general type-2 fuzzy systems to provide more robust interpretation to capture and manage the uncertainty presented in the data.

articleTitle: Towards Reconstructing the Filamentary Structure of an Only Partially Visible Cosmic Web with Deep Learning and 3D Cosmological Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: On large scales, the Universe forms a complex structure of filaments, walls, voids, and nodes known as cosmic web. It is known that a galaxy’s location in the cosmic web can change their properties and affect their evolutionary history. However, it can be difficult to detect these structures observationally, since filaments are sparsely traced out by the few galaxies that are visible along their length. We propose to train a CNN-based encoder-decoder model on 3D cosmological simulations where the true filamentary structure is known, but only a small number of the galaxies that trace it out can be detected. Preliminary results have been achieved by combining multiple deep learning techniques such as kernel design, pre-training and data augmentation. This has led to an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 7. 6 \%}$, precision of $33.0 \%$ and recall of $41.4 \%$, which in the context of the problem means success in identifying true negatives and room for improvement in true positives.

articleTitle: Kathakali Mudras: An AI-Enhanced Predictive Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: The goal of this research is to integrate an artificial intelligence framework for predicting Kathakali mudras, a crucial component of the traditional Indian dance style that is renowned for its complex hand and facial motions. Our goal is to protect and improve the accessibility of this traditional art form by utilising deep learning technology. To be more precise, we used the object identification model YOLOv8 together with convolutional neural networks (CNNs) like VGG 19, Inception V3, and ResNet 152 to predict and analyse Kathakali mudras. Furthermore, Few-shot learning (FSL) and support vector machines (SVMs) were used to offer a comparative viewpoint on the efficacy of machine learning method in this situation. The study entailed a thorough analysis of how well-performing different deep learning techniques performed. The predictive accuracy of VGG 19, Inception V3, and ResNet 152 for intricate mudras of Kathakali was subjected to a thorough evaluation process. In addition, an evaluation of YOLOv8’s real-time object identification capabilities was conducted in order to investigate its potential in live performance circumstances. The results of the experiment showed that VGG 19 performed better than the other models and had the highest accuracy in mudra prediction. As a result, VGG 19 was chosen as the best algorithm for this particular application. The results of this study demonstrate how artificial intelligence (AI) technologies may support and preserve traditional artistic forms. This AI-integrated framework is a useful tool for scholars, educators, and dancers, promoting a deeper knowledge and enjoyment of this cultural legacy through its accurate analysis and prediction of Kathakali mudras.

articleTitle: Geometric Optimization of a Trapezoidal microchannel Heat Sink Using the Grey Wolf Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Advanced cooling techniques are needed to manage high heat flow generated by minimizing electronic components in integrated circuits. To enhance the microchannel’s geometry and increase heat transfer efficiency, the optimization algorithm inspired by the gray wolf is suggested in this work. Three nondimensional design factors determine the trapezoidal microchannel heat sink, and this study evaluates thermal resistance and dissipation power as indicators of the heat sink. The research describes how to use the Non-Dominated Sorting Grey Wolf Optimizer (NSGWO) to formulate a two-objective numerical model in a multi-objective optimization. The proposed method offered a variety of optimal solutions striking a balance to determine the best geometric configuration and demonstrating a good alignment with existing optimization approaches.

articleTitle: Flood Risk Simulation and Mitigation in Coastal Areas: An ArcGIS Pro and Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: The integration of ArcGIS with Deep Learning models demonstrates a significant advancement in coastal flood prediction and prevention, offering enhanced accuracy and detail in flood risk mapping. Our suggested approach not only improves disaster preparedness and response but also holds promise for broader application across vulnerable coastal regions. Continued refinement and expansion of proposed model will further solidify its role as a critical tool in enhancing coastal flood resilience on a global scale. This study underscores the effectiveness of integrating ArcGIS with Deep Learning models for coastal flood prediction and prevention. The model—whether prioritizing precision, recall, or a balanced approach—offers unique advantages tailored to different application needs. The promising results highlight the potential of this integrated approach to significantly improve disaster preparedness and response in vulnerable coastal areas. Moving forward, further refinement and expansion of this methodology across diverse regions will strengthen its role in enhancing global coastal flood resilience.

articleTitle: Crime Prediction Using Spatial-Temporal Synchronous Graph Convolutional Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Crime prediction is an essential task for improving public safety and optimizing resource allocation. However, accurately forecasting crimes poses significant challenges due to the irregular spatial distributions of crime events and their dynamic temporal patterns. Traditional methods are limited in their ability to capture complex spatial-temporal dependencies. In this paper, we adapt the Spatial-Temporal Synchronous Graph Convolutional Network (STSGCN) to the crime prediction domain, where spatial-temporal relationships and cross-category crime influences are crucial. By leveraging both spatial graph convolutions and temporal convolutions simultaneously, STSGCN can model the intricate dependencies between crime occurrences across different regions and time periods. Our experimental results demonstrate that STSGCN outperforms these models in both crime occurrence prediction and crime frequency forecasting, providing a more robust framework for spatial-temporal crime prediction.

articleTitle: CanScan: Classification of cancer types using deep learning approach
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: In this research, an artificial intelligence (AI) model for the detection of tree types of cancer, cluster in benign and malignant, is presented. The main objective is to develop a precise and reliable classification system that can aid in early diagnosis and medical decision-making. The model utilizes deep learning techniques and is based on a carefully selected set of features extracted from medical images and relevant clinical data. To train and evaluate the model, a dataset of clinical data collected from cancer patients across different hospitals and medical centers was used. Data preprocessing techniques were applied to normalize and clean the data before feeding it into the AI model. A classification algorithm, such as a neural network, was implemented and trained using a deep learning approach. The model “InceptionV3” achieved an 87% accuracy on the validation set and was evaluated using standard performance metrics such as precision and sensitivity. The results obtained demonstrated high accuracy in detecting types of cancer, showcasing the effectiveness of the proposed model. Furthermore, comparisons were made with other existing cancer detection approaches in the scientific literature, and it was observed that the proposed model outperforms several of them in terms of accuracy and overall performance. This study not only represents a significant advancement in the field of cancer detection but also underscores the potential of artificial intelligence to transform the landscape of healthcare. It is expected that this model can enhance the accuracy and efficiency of diagnosis, thereby assisting healthcare professionals in clinical decision-making.

articleTitle: A Survey on Origin-Destination Flow Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Origin-Destination (OD) prediction is a widely studied area across various disciplines, including transportation, urban planning, and computer science. This survey provides a comprehensive review of OD prediction, covering theoretical foundations, practical challenges, and advanced computational models such as machine learning and deep learning. We examine key aspects like input features, model types, datasets, and evaluation metrics, highlighting the trade-offs between utility and performance, as well as the challenges of model interpretability and scalability across different applications. The advantages of modern machine learning and deep learning models, such as their ability to handle large-scale spatiotemporal data, are contrasted with their inherent complexity and computational cost. Finally, we identify current challenges and propose future directions, such as improving model scalability, enhancing interpretability, and integrating privacy-preserving mechanisms, aiming to bridge gaps across disciplines and promote integrated solutions for OD prediction.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Ensemble Stacking Method for Neurodegenarative Disease Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases present a current challenge in the accuracy of the diagnosis. Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s disease take a number of years to accurately define the growth of the disease. Neural networks are very efficient algorithm to handle the image data. This paper proposes an ensemble stacking method for the classification of Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, and Normal using MRI images. And also compare the performance with other neural networks such as deep neural networks, convolutional neural networks, and VGG16. The proposed model got a better accuracy of $\mathbf{9 4 \%}$ than other neural network models.

articleTitle: Multi-Disease Detection and Classification of Sugarcane Leaves using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: The early detection of multiple diseases in sugarcane is crucial for improving crop yield and reducing losses. Traditional manual inspection methods are time-consuming, errorprone, and require expert knowledge. In this study, we propose a novel approach for detecting multiple diseases in sugarcane leaves using a combination of transfer learning and a custom hybrid model. Initially, pre-trained models like MobileNet and DenseNet are fine-tuned on a sugarcane disease dataset to leverage the feature extraction capabilities of transfer learning. We then propose a new model, the MobileNet-DenseNet Concatenation (MobileNet-DenseNet Concat), which combines the strengths of both architectures. This hybrid model fuses the lightweight, efficient nature of MobileNet with the deep feature extraction capabilities of DenseNet, creating a robust model for multidisease classification. The model is trained and evaluated on a labeled sugarcane disease dataset, and its performance is compared with individual transfer learning models. The proposed model achieves improved $96 \%$ accuracy, precision, recall, and F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> scores, outperforming existing approaches in detecting multiple diseases simultaneously. Additionally, techniques like bounding boxes are used to localize disease regions on the leaves. The results demonstrate that the MobileNet-DenseNet Concat model offers a promising solution for automating sugarcane disease detection, potentially benefiting farmers and agronomists by facilitating early intervention and treatment strategies.

articleTitle: SecureMed: Federated learning empowered approach for securing medical data
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: In today’s era, the world is suffering from an infectious disease COVID-19 which proved to be health predicament. The COVID-19 testing data is being produced by the healthcare center at preeminent scale. The efficient handling of such data by World Health Organization (WHO) team and medical practitioners is the considerable challenge. The researchers have introduced many deep learning approaches to detect COVID-19, but security remained challenging. In this paper, we present federated learning based approach ‘SecureMed,’ which allows to securely process the data. In this approach, two parameters, ‘client selection’ and ‘aggregation method’ are considered. The proposed scheme inherits Markov model for designing the these two parameters. The approach is been validated by using publicly available COVID-19 dataset of size 771, 634 Genomes (source: NCBI, U.S. National Library of Medicine). Taking into account the probability computations, the proposed approach succeeds in client local training by 50%.

articleTitle: Antelope classification using Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Reliable and efficient monitoring of animals in their natural habitat is crucial to inform management and conservation decisions. Automation of species classification is important since manually classifying animals is expensive, monotonous, and time-consuming. Current studies have shown that Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are effective at animal classification tasks. However, there is little research on distinguishing species like antelopes from each other. In this paper, an implementation of Deep Neural Networks in the classification of antelopes is proposed. Our model achieved a 93% Top-1 accuracy on the dataset, which is higher than most of the models discussed in the literature. This paper shows that DNNs, specifically vision transformers, can accurately classify antelopes. Out-of-distribution modelling using softmax confidence was implemented and an accuracy of 74% after introducing an out-of-distribution sample to the test dataset was achieved. Further work can be done to classify species like the lesser Kudu or Greater Kudu, which is more complex than the work of this study. For the out-of-distribution modelling, methods like using the energy score can also be explored to improve the accuracy.

articleTitle: Recent Technologies in Differential Privacy for NLP Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Differential Privacy (DP) has become a crucial framework for preserving data privacy, especially in the field of Natural Language Processing (NLP). This survey provides a comprehensive overview of existing DP applications in NLP, focusing on key aspects such as application scenario classification, diversity of privacy mechanisms, utility-performance trade-offs, data granularity, empirical studies versus theoretical analysis, and emerging challenges with future directions.

articleTitle: q-rung orthopair neutrosophic fuzzy rough sets with an application based on multi-criteria decision-making
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Fuzzy set theory, introduced in the 1960s, has grown significantly through various generalizations, including intuitionistic, pythagorean, and fermatean fuzzy sets. These extensions enhance the theory’s flexibility in managing uncertainty. Also, q-rung orthopair fuzzy sets extend these concepts by broadening the scope of hesitation, offering a more versatile tool for decision-making. Neutrosophic fuzzy sets further incorporate three membership degrees—truth, indeterminacy, and falsity to handle uncertainty better. Meanwhile, rough set theory excels at addressing indiscernibility through relations and approximations. Combining these strengths, q-rung orthopair neutrosophic fuzzy rough sets are introduced in this paper. Based on the proposed theory, an algorithm is designed to rank the alternatives based on various criteria and then an application is discussed, where a student uses the proposed theory to choose the best university from the given choices.

articleTitle: Industrial computed tomography based intelligent non-destructive testing method for power capacitor
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Power capacitor device is a widely used reactive power compensation equipment in power transmission and distribution system which can easily have internal fault and therefore affects the safe operation of the power system. An intelligent non-destructive testing (I-NDT) method based on ICT is proposed to test the quality of power capacitors automatically in this study. The internal structure of power capacitors would be scanned by the ICT device and then defects could be recognized by the SSD algorithm. Moreover, the data augmentation algorithm is used to extend the image set to improve the stability and accuracy of the trained SSD model.

articleTitle: A Multi-level Classification Assisted Evolutionary Algorithm Based on Distribution Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: In decomposition-based multi-objective evolutionary algorithms (MOEAs), a set of uniformly distributed reference vectors is employed to decompose a multi-objective problem into different subproblems, and solutions are selected based on various subproblem evaluation functions. However, during the solution selection process, there is a tendency for individuals to be assigned to subproblems associated with reference vectors that are relatively distant. This can lead to the exclusion of individuals with better convergence properties if they are far from the reference vectors, resulting in wasted solutions and reduced convergence speed of the population.To address this issue and retain individuals with better convergence properties while using a classification surrogate to select higher-quality candidates for actual evaluation, this paper introduces an algorithm that incorporates a distribution prediction-based multi-layer classification surrogate model. This model effectively resolves the problem of improper individual solution allocation in traditional decomposition-based MOEAs. By optimizing classification and regression models, the proposed algorithm demonstrates improved convergence and solution quality in multi-objective optimization problems. Experimental results indicate that our proposed algorithm outperforms comparative algorithms on most of the test problems.

articleTitle: Retrained Model as a Pillar for an Automatic NPK Analyzer
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Image classification is utilized across various disciplines. This study applied image classification to the assigned colors of Nitrogen, Phosphorous, and Potassium. Specifically, it answered the following questions: 1) What are the features to be considered to classify Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium? 2) What is the performance of the inception-v3 in terms of Training Accuracy, Validation Accuracy, and Cross-entropy; and 3) What is the percentile prediction and how much time is needed to analyze a Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium image? Based on the results, The color coding of soil nutrient levels makes it easy for users to determine the acidity of soil. The Inception V3 model has a 100% Training Accuracy, and 100% Validation Accuracy on the images of Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium. Moreover, it posted a Cross-entropy of $\mathbf{0 . 0 0 3}$ for $\mathbf{N}, \mathbf{0 . 0 0 7}$ for P, and $\mathbf{. 0 0 2}$ for K; and the percentile prediction and time needed to analyze a nitrogen image is $\mathbf{9 8 . 2 6 2 \%}$ in 4.82 seconds, a phosphorus image is $\mathbf{9 7 . 4 2 1 \%}$ in 4.64 seconds, and a K image is $99.684 \%$ in 4.80 seconds. The assigned NPK colors can be used to automatically determine the presence or level of soil nutrients. The color coding of soil nutrient levels makes it easy for image classifier models to determine the acidity of soil. 20 images in each of the NPK labels are enough to retrain the Inception V3. The Inception V3 model can be easily used as the backbone for image classification software. It is highly recommended for novice AI developers.

articleTitle: Optimized Image Watermarking Scheme using Ant Colony Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: The trend of sharing digital content over the Internet exposes it to various risks that can compromise its authenticity, integrity, and ownership rights. As a result, robust watermarking schemes have emerged to address these concerns while respecting Digital Rights Management (DRM) protection measures. These schemes enable the secure transmission of copyrighted content and digital data. This paper presents a unique investigation into a watermarking scheme that integrates Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) with Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) in Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) domain for digital images. The objective is to incorporate the watermark in the coefficients of host images in such a manner that it is visually imperceptible and preserves the robustness of the watermarking scheme. For this purpose, we have employed multiple scaling factors for embedding the watermark. Our experimentation involves four grayscale host images, and we compare the proposed watermarking scheme against other techniques in same domain. The results validate that our approach surpasses alternative methods, satisfying all the necessary criteria for an optimized and resilient watermarking solution.

articleTitle: Voice Modulation in Audiobook Narration
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: In today’s world, most audiobooks lack emotional depth, which hinders listeners from enjoying the story. This study delves into voice modulation techniques based on emotion as a means to improve audiobook narration by using machine learning algorithms along with text-to-speech (TTS) technology, thereby enhancing the overall storytelling experience. This study hopes to contribute to the intricate interplay between voice modulation techniques and audience perception, paving the way for further research and refinement in audiobook narration.

articleTitle: Road Lane Tracking Using Constrained Scale Space Radon Transform
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: On a road, there are often parallel linear structures painted in white or color to demarcate the lanes. For automatic driving, these structures must be tracked in image sequences acquired in real time by an embedded camera so that a vehicle can stay in its lane or change lanes. These road markings appear in grayscale images as continuous or discontinuous linear structures of variable width, converging at vanishing points. In this article, we propose tracking these road markings using both the Scale Space Radon Transform (SSRT) and projective geometry. These markings are considered as a mixture of linear structures, with the model being updated under parallelism constraints. The proposed multiline tracker is less sensitive to noise and acquisition conditions due to simultaneous adjustment expressed in feature space. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of SSRT and the simultaneous tracking of multiple lines.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Powered Mobile Application For Early Skin Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: This research work presents the development and implementation of a skin scan app utilizing deep learning technologies. The aim is to provide users with a convenient and accessible tool for skin analysis to reduce the reliance on traditional dermatological solutions. After extensive exploration of different deep learning techniques, an efficient and accurate model, EffecientNetB0V2 was identified as the most suitable model and trained using the HAM10000 skin cancer dataset. The developed models were then integrated into a user-friendly flutter application called “SkinKo” that is fully developed from scratch, and designed to offer an intuitive and seamless experience for users. This research not only showcases the technical aspects of developing such an application but also focuses on the potential impact on the healthcare community. By offering an “in-pocket dermatologist” This application has the potential to empower users to monitor their skin health more effectively and seek timely medical attention when necessary.

articleTitle: MAS4CHICKEN: Multi-Agent Systems based order service model for waiting time reduction at rotisserie chicken restaurants in Lima - Peru
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: A very frequent problem at rotisserie chicken restaurants in Lima - Peru is the diners’ long waiting times. This generates discomfort on the diners, as well as negative reviews towards these kinds of restaurants. There are studies out there that aim to combat this issue by using simulating software such as Arena, Promodel, AnyLogic, etc. However, this article uses a different method called “Multi-Agent Systems (MAS)”. In order to combat the aforementioned issue, the MAS4CHICKEN model has been created, which aims to determine the optimal scenario in which the diners are attended with the lowest delay possible, allowing for the diners to feel satisfied. This implemented method mainly uses three different kinds of agents: Waiter, Chef, and Diner. This model was developed with the NetLogo modeling software, which makes it easier to work on Multi-Agent Systems and their characteristic behaviors. The proposed model was tested under different scenarios. By the end of the tests it was concluded that 4 chefs are able to optimally attend diners that come by every 5 minutes, resulting in an attention time of 13.76 minutes. Additionally, it was determined that the model allows the user to evaluate strategies and measure the impact of its implementation in a virtual environment. While this model was firstly designed for rotisserie chicken restaurants, it can be used, either as-is or extended, to work with different kinds of restaurants.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal MRI Brain Tumor Segmentation Using Attention Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Gliomas are one of the most aggressive brain tumors which can be a potential threat to life in their advanced stages. Manual detection of brain tumor is computationally expensive. Therefore, timely and precise localization of such tumors is crucial for diagnosis and further treatments. This study demonstrates the deployment of Attention Modules (AMs) in the baseline nnUNet (AM-nnUNet) for multi-sequence MRI brain tumor segmentation to achieve state-of-the-art performance. The AM-nnUNet utilizes BraTS 2020 dataset for training and validation using 5 -fold cross-validation (CV), exploring several variants incorporating Focal Tversky loss function (FTL), aggressive data augmentation (DA) techniques, and group normalization (GN) instead of instance normalization. Comprehensive experiments were carried out on BraTS dataset for different variant of proposed AM-nnUNet: AM-nnUNet + FTL, AM-nnUNet + FTL + DA, AM-nnUNet + FTL +GN and AMnnUNet + FTL +GN+DA. Experimental findings suggest AMnnUNet + FTL + GN + DA outperformed other AM-nnUNet varaints. AM-nnUNet + FTL + GN + DA, achieved dice scores of $0.9025,0.9387$, and 0.9568 for enhancing tumor (ET), necrotic tumor core (NC), and peritumoral edematous/invaded tissue (ED) labels, respectively. Comparative analyses were conducted with state-of-the art CNN architectures and nn-UNet based frameworks demonstrated that proposed framework yielded better segmentation performance.

articleTitle: Research on Trajectory Planning of Denture Milling Machine Tools
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: In the current era of rapidly advancing global technology, characterized by deep integration and rapid progress in materials science, information technology, and intelligent manufacturing, the international high-end manufacturing sector is undergoing unprecedented transformation and upgrading. The swift development of high-end manufacturing technology and society’s strong pursuit of quality of life have presented new opportunities for the dental prosthetic manufacturing industry. However, traditional dental milling machine technology is no longer able to meet increasingly stringent accuracy requirements and consumes significant energy, thereby limiting the industry’s development. This study involves reconstructing and optimizing STL file topology using both triangular mesh topology algorithms and half-edge topology algorithms. It accurately determines tool positions through curve fitting utilizing the least squares method. Additionally, it employs NURBS algorithms to generate tool paths and designs specific algorithms to reduce path redundancy, thus improving machining efficiency. Simulation experiments demonstrate that the proposed trajectory optimization algorithm effectively reduces milling time by 68 seconds and decreases energy consumption by $10 \%$. This research provides theoretical support for innovative development and practical application of dental milling machine technology.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Sequential Deep Learning Models in Financial Time Series Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Time series analysis of daily stock prices is challenging due to the inherent complexity, nonlinearity, and nonstationarity of financial data. In this paper, we compare three sequential deep learning models—LSTM, Transformer, and Large Language Models (LLMs)—for stock price prediction. By transforming the regression problem of predicting daily log returns into a classification task, we evaluate the models’ classification accuracies, with the Transformer achieving the highest accuracy of 22%, followed by LSTM (15.6%) and LLM (15.3%). Regression metrics showed LSTM initially performing better, with a lower RMSE (180.92) than LLM (1739.61). However, outlier predictions in the LLM, caused by incomplete number outputs, inflated its error. After removing these outliers, LLM’s RMSE improved significantly to 33.85, surpassing LSTM. These results demonstrate the potential of Transformer and LLM models for financial time series prediction. Future work will explore incorporating self-reflection mechanisms in LLM predictions and extending the comparison to multivariate financial time series incorporating textual data and other features.

articleTitle: Android Malware Detection Using Ensemble Learning and Feature Selection with Insights from SHAP Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: The increasing proliferation of Android mobile devices, along with a surge in malware targeting these platforms, underscores the need for advanced malware detection methods. This research introduces a robust approach to Android malware detection by employing ensemble learning techniques. The integration of Random Forest, XGBoost, Extremely Randomized Trees, and Histogram-based Gradient Boosting models forms the core of the proposed method. Enhancing this approach, feature selection is performed using Random Forest Feature Importance, focusing on the most relevant features to achieve high accuracy and efficiency. Additionally, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) Explainable AI is utilized to provide transparency and a comprehensive understanding of the model’s decisions, thereby fostering user trust and comprehension. The proposed method was evaluated on the CICMalDroid2020 dataset, demonstrating superior performance, with XGBoost achieving the highest accuracy at $\mathbf{9 4. 8 8 \%}$. This research not only advances the field of malware detection on Android devices but also contributes significantly to the explanation and interpretation of machine learning models within the context of cybersecurity.

articleTitle: F-Detector: Design of a Solution Based on Machine Learning to Detect Logical Fallacias on Digital Texts
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: The design of F-Detector, as an improved Machine Learning-based solution aimed at detecting logical fallacies in digital texts. Using an advanced NLP approach based on BERT, enhances the classification of text fragments into various categories of logical fallacies by incorporating more robust linguistic features and a more accurate classification model. The performance of F-Detector was rigorously evaluated using multiple metrics, demonstrating an overall precision of $75 \%$, significantly improving upon the $18 \%$ precision achieved by previous solutions. Additionally, this model will be integrated into a Chrome extension, allowing users, including educators, researchers, and the general public, to utilize it in a natural way. This enhanced tool has the potential for broad application in education and digital content analysis, contributing to better discourse quality and more effective misinformation detection.

articleTitle: LusTra: waste type prediction through sound and accelerometer data
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: In recent years, advancements in waste sorting have been significantly enhanced by the integration of deep learning algorithms. In this regard, LusTra proposes a waste type recognition system using sound and accelerometer data. Two waste types are considered: Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) bottles and Aluminium cans. Predictions through sound data, converted to Mel spectrograms, with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), are promising and result in an accuracy of ${8 9 \%}$ for PET waste and ${9 0 \%}$ for aluminium waste. Random forest with features extracted from the accelerometer data provide an accuracy of ${7 6 \%}$ and $86 \%$ for PET and aluminium respectively.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning Utilizing Real Industrial Vehicle Data Based on Similar Usage Trends
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: This study proposed a lifespan prediction method for fuel-cell systems in industrial vehicles within the framework of transfer learning. Since industrial vehicles with fuel cells have only recently become widely used, there is a dearth of data per vehicle. Additionally, the use of such vehicles differs among customers. Under these constraints, the model prediction by ridge regression showed that some vehicles missed the prediction significantly. Therefore, to achieve more consistent performance across vehicles, we considered a transfer learning method for applying knowledge from the data of other vehicles. Specifically, as an extension of ridge regression, we propose a regularization term that transfers knowledge from other vehicle data and grouping method for creating a group of similar vehicles. Validations on a real dataset of vehicles in operation showed that the proposed method reduces the standard deviation of prediction error by $31 \%$ compared with ridge regression. In particular, 58% reduction is observed for vehicles with large prediction error. Furthermore, the proposed method also reduces the average prediction error by $16 \%$ compared with ridge regression. This study contributes to improving operating efficiency by enhancing the accuracy of lifespan predictions for fuel-cell systems in industrial vehicles and advancing time-series prediction technology.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Enhancing Fine-Tuning of Pre-trained Language Models for Sentiment Analysis Using Metaheuristic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Fine-tuning pre-trained language models for specific natural language processing tasks often leads to suboptimal performance due to the vast parameter space and the challenge of finding the most effective model configurations. Traditional fine-tuning methods can be computationally expensive and may not fully exploit the potential of these models, particularly for tasks like sentiment analysis. This work explores the application of metaheuristic techniques, focusing on sentiment analysis using the Stanford Sentiment Treebank 2 (SST2) dataset.We utilize two approaches: Genetic Algorithms (GA) and the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA). These methods aim to efficiently search the parameter space and optimize the fine-tuning process of pretrained language models. To enhance efficiency, we incorporate layer freezing techniques along with different crossover strategies. In the results obtained, GA with Simulated Binary Crossover (SBX) and 30% layer freezing achieved 94.02% accuracy, while WOA with SBX crossover and 30% layer freezing achieved 94.67% accuracy. These outcomes highlight the potential of integrating evolutionary algorithms, nature-inspired optimization techniques, and strategic layer freezing with deep learning finetuning processes for NLP tasks.

articleTitle: Advanced Stock Price Prediction with xLSTM-Based Models: Improving Long-Term Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Stock price prediction has long been a critical area of research in financial modeling. The inherent complexity of financial markets, characterized by both short-term fluctuations and long-term trends, poses significant challenges in accurately capturing underlying patterns. While Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks have shown strong performance in short-term stock price prediction, they struggle with effectively modeling long-term dependencies. In this paper, we propose an advanced stock price prediction model based on the Extended Long Short-Term Memory (xLSTM) algorithm, designed to enhance predictive accuracy over both short and long-term periods. We conduct extensive experiments by building and evaluating models based on xLSTM and LSTM architectures for multiple stocks. Our results demonstrate that the xLSTM model consistently outperforms the LSTM model across all stocks and time horizons, with the performance gap widening as the prediction period extends. The observations underscore the superior capability of the xLSTM-based model to capture long-term patterns in financial data, offering a promising approach for more accurate and reliable stock price predictions.

articleTitle: Enhancing Deepfake Detection with a Hybrid CNN-BiLSTM Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Rapid improvements in deepfake technology have created serious threats to the integrity of digital information. Deepfakes have the potential to be employed for intimidating or blackmailing specific public figures, as well as for deceiving the general public. Concurrently, the advancement in deepfake technology has led to notable progress in developing detection algorithms. Primarily, these algorithms concentrate on analyzing images rather than delving into the temporal progression within video content. In the information era of today, detecting deepfakes has become more important than ever. The paper posits a pioneering hybrid approach for detecting deepfake videos, combining the scrutiny of human eye blinking patterns, utilizing Xception image characteristics, and implementing a Bidirectional Long Short Term Memory network (Bi-LSTM). This methodology leverages Convolutional Neural Networks(CNN) to extract image attributes and Bi-LSTM networks to scrutinize sequences consecutively. Moreover, it utilizes an adaptive spatio-temporal attention mechanism to concentrate on pertinent frames in the video sequences. The dataset used for experimental purposes includes both authentic and artificially generated videos from the Celeb-DF dataset. The proposed framework attained an accuracy rate of 86% in classification with an area under curve of 0.90, showcasing its efficacy in the identification of deepfake videos.

articleTitle: A data classification technique that provides qualitative and quantitative information inspired by the chromatographic separation method of substances
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Currently, there are several significant limitations in the issues related to the exploration of large data sets using classical classification methods, the results of which are used in the decision-making process. The first significant limitation in the use of classical classification methods is the need to ensure a constant size of the data. The second type of limitation is related to the dimension of the data. The last type of limitation that occurs when using classical classification algorithms is related to the situation that a given input vector may contain data belonging to many classes simultaneously. On the other hand, as a result of processing large data sets, we want to obtain not only qualitative information, but also quantitative information, which is equally important in the decision-making process. It seems that one of the methods of solving the above problems in data classification is the adaptation of classification mechanisms used, for example, in analytical chemistry to identify complex chemical compounds in the tested mixture. The article proposes an innovative algorithm for the classification of multidimensional data based on the chromatographic separation method. The article presents a distributed data classification algorithm based on the gas chromatography technique, which in issues related to the classification of large data sets is not subject to the above limitations and provides quantitative and qualitative information. The article also presents the classification results of the algorithm for selected - standard data sets. This work shows that based on the proposed chromatographic separation method, we also obtain quantitative information, not only qualitative information, which is a significant advantage in comparison to classical classification methods.

articleTitle: Extreme Value Modelling of Feature Residuals for Anomaly Detection in Dynamic Graphs
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Detecting anomalies in a temporal sequence of graphs can be applied is areas such as the detection of accidents in transport networks and cyber attacks in computer networks. Existing methods for detecting abnormal graphs can suffer from multiple limitations, such as high false positive rates as well as difficulties with handling variable-sized graphs and non-trivial temporal dynamics. To address this, we propose a technique where temporal dependencies are explicitly modelled via time series analysis of a large set of pertinent graph features, followed by using residuals to remove the dependencies. Extreme Value Theory is then used to robustly model and classify any remaining extremes, aiming to produce low false positives rates. Comparative evaluations on a multitude of graph instances show that the proposed approach obtains considerably better accuracy than TensorSplat and Laplacian Anomaly Detection.

articleTitle: Beyond Words: Memetic Theory as a Lens to Expose Ideological Bias in Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: This study builds upon existing research examining ideological propagation and the integration of memetic theories within Language Models (LMs). We investigated four memetic hypotheses in LMs - competition among ‘selfish memes’, the presence of memeplexes, the varying susceptibility of agents, and the influence of human guardrails. We fine-tuned twelve LMs on the MediaNLP dataset, derived from GPT-2 and DistilBERT base models, across thematic subsets of religion, politics, and opinions on AI. Subsequently, we conducted seven experiments in an attempt to disprove three null hypotheses. These experiments included measuring the variation between the models and human ground truth, evaluating the effects of exposure to AI-generated content using epidemiological modeling, analyzing cosine distances among key words in LM embeddings, applying cryptographic benchmarks, and scrutinizing changes in model weights and biases. We disproved Null Hypothesis I, but did not disprove Null Hypotheses II and III. Furthermore, our findings underscore the significant role of human designers in shaping the guardrails of ChatGPT, particularly in generating data containing potentially ‘sensitive’ content. This study represents a novel investigation in applying memetic theory to highlight potential unexplored risks and vulnerabilities inherent in LMs and their output.

articleTitle: A Generative Frailty Index based Explainable Approach for Hospital Readmission Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: A reliable and transparent prediction model for hospital readmission is essential to decrease unexpected costs and improve patient’s health. This research proposes a novel comprehensive approach that leverages a generative AI mechanism to extract Frailty Index (FI) features for predicting hospital readmission by utilizing diverse data types. Our approach calculates FI using both structured data and detailed clinical notes, ensuring a more accurate reflection of clinical assessments, and addressing the limitations of existing models regarding both explainability and data diversity. The proposed approach provides an explainable framework that aligns with real-life clinical decision-making processes, identifying key factors contributing to readmission risk. It has significant implications for healthcare professionals, researchers, and policymakers, with the potential to improve patient outcomes, reduce healthcare costs, and enhance the overall quality of care. Our findings demonstrate the value of generative AI and the use of FI in providing transparent and accurate predictions, offering valuable explanations and reasoning behind predictive modeling.

articleTitle: Traffic Incident Reasoning Through Multi-Grained Conceptual Graph Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: The paper proposes a novel Conceptual Graph Reasoning Network (CGR) for analyzing traffic events in videos, which is crucial for autonomous vehicles, assisted driving, and intelligent transportation systems (ITS). CGR focuses on Visual Question Answering (VQA) at the event level by integrating spatial-temporal and linguistic representations using graph convolution networks. It includes a Diversity-aware Conceptual Reasoning (DCR) module that separates misleading correlations and dynamically adjusts the importance of different features. The CGR’s effectiveness is demonstrated using the SUTD-TrafficQA dataset, showing significant performance improvements through ablation studies.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Approach To Face Shape Classification For Hairstyle, Beauty And Eyewear Recommendations
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Accurate face shape classification plays an important role in the growing field of personalized recommendations for hairstyle, beauty, and eyewear designs. Face shape classification is a computer vision task which aims to identify the shape of a human face from an image. This paper introduces state-of-the-art deep learning approaches for accurate face shape classification using advanced convolutional neural networks (CNNs) such as GoogLeNet, MobileNetV3, ResNet50, and Sequential CNN. The system analyses images of faces with varying shapes, such as - oval, round, square, heart, and oblong and provides personalized recommendations. The results of the study shows that GoogLeNet achieves the highest accuracy at ${9 1 . 0 3 \%}$, followed by MobileNetV3 at ${8 9 . 7 4 \%}$, ResNet50 at ${8 8 . 5 4 \%}$, and the Sequential CNN at ${8 0 . 0 2 \%}$. The superior performance of GoogLeNet indicates its efficacy in capturing the intricate features necessary for precise face shape classification. Additionally, a Flask-based web application has been developed, which enables real-time face shape classification and provides personalized recommendations.

articleTitle: Network Traffic Forecasting via Fuzzy Spatial-Temporal Fusion Graph Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Spatial-temporal network traffic prediction remains a formidable challenge due to the intricate spatial relationships and dynamic temporal patterns characteristic of individual nodes. Traditional regression methods fall short in handling such graph-structured data effectively. In recent developments, Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown promise in modeling these complex spatial-temporal interactions. Despite their potential, existing GNN-based approaches exhibit notable limitations: (1) they typically rely on fixed spatial adjacency matrices, which overlook fuzzy latent temporal dependencies; and (2) they often process spatial and temporal information independently, resulting in a loss of joint fuzzy dependencies or restricting the model to either global or local patterns alone. To overcome these issues, we introduce the Fuzzy Spatial-Temporal Fusion Graph Neural Network (FSTFGNN) based on Fuzzy Rough Sets. Our approach constructs a dynamic, data-driven fuzzy spatial-temporal fusion matrix to capture underlying low-level spatial-temporal joint relationships. Additionally, a fuzzy global-local unified GNN layer is incorporated to simultaneously learn global-local spatialtemporal dependencies. Experimental results on two real-world datasets validate the efficacy of the proposed FSTFGNN framework.

articleTitle: Dataset generation and model fine-tuning for GUI anomaly detection
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: In the rapidly evolving smartphone industry, ensuring the quality and usability of mobile applications is crucial, particularly through robust Graphical User Interfaces. Traditional manual GUI testing methods no longer support the complexity of modern applications. This paper presents a methodology for GUI anomaly detection leveraging synthetic data generation and deep learning. Our approach addresses the limitations of existing methods by creating a dataset that accurately replicates real-world GUI anomalies, such as cropped text, overlapping elements, pixelation, and null values. We used the dataset generated to train and evaluate the well-known YOLOv8 model, attaining 97% mAP to recognize the anomalies. Our study underscores the potential of automated, scalable solutions for automated enhancing GUI testing.

articleTitle: Gold Price Forecasting in Uncertain Times: Integrating Sentiment Analysis and External Indices
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: Since 2020, financial markets have experienced unprecedented volatility, making the traditional models for predicting gold prices significantly challenging. These models often overlook the nuanced impacts of real-time sentiment, economic indicators, and related metals like silver.
