This study proposes a novel framework to combine gold prices with other relevant features to improve predictive performance in the precious metal market. Further, we employ three advanced recent deep learning models, LSTM, N-HiTS, and TSMixer, and evaluate their performance with various metrics using the different combinations of the proposed features. The results demonstrate that incorporating the proposed additional features, such as silver prices and sentiment analysis, significantly improves forecasting accuracy, amidst the volatile and uncertain market conditions spanning from 2020 to 2024. The best-performing models outperform traditional models, such as ARIMA. Our findings highlight the importance of feature selection and combination in predictive modeling and demonstrate the potential of multi-feature models in capturing complex market dynamics. The insights from this study can inform investment decisions and risk management strategies in the precious metal market, and future research can build on our approach to explore additional features and models.

articleTitle: TAP: Transformers Driven Adaptive Prefetching for Hybrid Memory Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: In the rapidly evolving landscape of hybrid memory systems, which integrate different types of memory, optimizing cache management is vital for achieving high performance and efficiency. Traditional prefetching techniques often struggle to adapt to modern systems’ dynamic and complex I/O access patterns. This paper proposes a novel machine learning-based cache replacement framework tailored for hybrid memory architectures. Our framework leverages advanced transformerbased sequence-to-sequence models to analyze historical access patterns and make data-driven cache management decisions. By continuously learning from past access behavior and adapting to real-time workload changes, our system enhances cache hit rates, reduces latency, and optimizes storage performance. Our Transformer-based adaptive prefetching approach addresses the problem of predicting within large address spaces and shows significant improvements over traditional (Stride) and machine learning (ML) based (Markov Chains, Long Short Term Memory) prefetchers, achieving hit ratios of 0.71, 0.91, and 0.47 for mixed, streaming, and random access workloads. It yields 16-64% improvements across various traces and settings by capturing complex contextual relationships and adapting to dynamic access patterns, enhancing hybrid memory systems and enabling efficient, scalable storage management in modern computing environments.

articleTitle: Proposing a Physical Condition Detection System by using RGB and Thermal Images for Facial Features Detection and Facial Temperature Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: This paper presents a system for identifying and predicting the physical condition of construction workers such as tiredness, drowsiness, and body temperature using face detection technology. We describe a device that captures both thermal and RGB images of a worker’s face simultaneously by using a thermal camera for thermal images and a web camera for RGB images. While detecting faces from RGB images can be straightforward using the existing technologies, detecting faces from thermal images is more challenging. By analyzing the thermal images taken from the thermal camera, we extract the temperature of the worker’s body. To measure the facial skin temperature remotely, there is a method using thermography. Facial skin temperature is an important indicator for assessing drowsiness and mental stress. Therefore, it is essential to automatically detect the face in the thermal image and extract the facial skin temperature. Previously, many studies have been done to detect faces from thermography, but it was a thermal image that showed a person without a background. Therefore, we proposed a new method using SSD (Single Shot Multibox Detector) to detect faces from thermal images in real environments such as offices. For practical application, we evaluated the detection accuracy based on the difference in the size of the face area in the thermal image. In addition, the temperature of facial ROI was extracted using the facial feature points obtained by using AAM (Active Appearance Model). As a result, the face detection accuracy using SSD was about $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$, and the temperature value of the face RoI (Region of Interest) could be extracted only when the error in the facial feature point was minimal.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Sorting Algorithms: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: In the realm of computer science, sorting algorithms play a pivotal role in optimising data organisation and retrieval processes across various applications. This paper presents a comprehensive examination and comparative analysis of the most commonly used sorting algorithms, focusing on their time, space complexity, and efficiency. By scrutinising both traditional methods like bubble sort, selection sort, and insertion sort, and advanced techniques such as merge sort, quick sort, heap sort, and radix sort, this study sheds light on the performance metrics of each algorithm. Through meticulous implementation and evaluation across datasets of varying magnitudes, ranging from 100 to 100,000 integers, the research provides valuable insights into the strengths and weaknesses of these sorting techniques. The outcomes of this study offer practical guidance for professionals in data engineering and software development, aiding in the informed selection of sorting algorithms tailored to specific application needs. Utilising a rigorous experimental setup with the pseudocode, the study meticulously measures the time complexity of each algorithm, recording CPU time in seconds. The analysis reveals significant performance differentials among the algorithms, showcasing the efficiency of quick sort, shell sort, and heap sort on small datasets, while highlighting the scalability of merge sort, radix sort, and quick sort as dataset sizes increase. This research contributes to the advancement of algorithmic knowledge and provides a valuable resource for practitioners seeking to optimise sorting processes in their computational tasks.

articleTitle: ML-Driven Audit Risk Assessment with Differential Privacy
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: In contemporary auditing practices, the ability to effectively identify and assess potential fraudulent companies is crucial for maintaining market fairness and transparency. Previous research has leveraged various machine learning techniques to detect fraudulent activities in financial data. However, these models often lack robustness and fail to protect the privacy of the financial information used for training. Here we introduces a novel approach by incorporating differential privacy into the training process, ensuring data protection without compromising model performance. To enhance model performance, we employed interquartile range filtering for outlier removal and optimized feature selection using Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Principal Component Analysis (PCA). For model training, we employed Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Decision Trees, with hyperparameters meticulously fine-tuned through grid search and Bayesian optimization techniques to achieve optimal performance. To address privacy concerns, we implemented differential privacy using the Laplace mechanism, effectively safeguarding sensitive financial data. Our empirical results demonstrate that the enhanced models maintain high accuracy and robustness, providing a reliable tool for fraud detection while ensuring financial data privacy.

articleTitle: Semi-supervised clustering algorithm for data streams
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Soft Computing & Machine Intelligence (ISCMI)
abstract: In many real-life applications, the existing data cannot be stored in a computer’s random access memory, requiring learning algorithms to process the data as streams. In some cases, limited information about the data set is available, which can be used to enhance learning outcomes. In semisupervised clustering (SSC), such information is presented as pairwise constraints in the form of “cannot-link” and “mustlink” constraints. This paper develops a SSC algorithm for data streams. We consider the data as a sequence of blocks and use a nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization model for the SSC problems. The algorithm is designed to process one block of data at each iteration. Special procedures are developed to identify cluster-determining points, which are used in subsequent iterations. The proposed algorithm is evaluated using some real-world data sets.
